summary: In Greek mythology, Tiphys (Ancient Greek: Τῖφυς) was the first helmsman of the Argo, a Thespian (Boeotian) pilot famed for reading sun, stars, and weather. Athena herself urged him to join Jason's crew; he steered the ship until he died of illness among the Mariandyni, after which Ancaeus took the helm.
etymology: Ancient Greek Tîphus (Τῖφυς). Parentage varies: son of Hagnias in Apollonius, or of Phorbas of Elis and Hyrmine in other lists.

sections.heading: Family
paragraphs: Tiphys is usually the Thespian son of Hagnias, or else of Phorbas of Elis and Hyrmine, daughter of Epeius — in the latter account a possible brother of Augeas and Actor. He left the Siphaean people of the Thespians to sail with the Argonauts.

sections.heading: Pilot of the Argo
paragraphs: Apollonius of Rhodes presents him as skilled to foretell rising waves and to infer stormy winds from sun and star; Tritonian Athena herself urged him to join the chiefs, and he came among them a welcome comrade. Later epic (Valerius Flaccus, Statius, the Orphic Argonautica) likewise places him at the tiller, watching the heavens and guiding the vessel through dangerous seas.

sections.heading: Death
paragraphs: On the voyage toward Colchis he died of a mysterious illness in the land of the Mariandynians — or, in some accounts, of a snakebite. After his death Ancaeus (son of Poseidon) piloted the Argo in his place.
